concept: Total count strategies for paginated UIs
summary: Source-anchored research for Total count strategies for paginated UIs. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: When a UI needs the exact number of documents matching its active filters, use `countDocuments(filter)` independently of the page fetch. MongoDB defines it as counting query matches, and Mongoose's pagination example runs `find(filter)` and `countDocuments(filter)` in parallel. (high confidence)

For sequential cursor or keyset interfaces, an exact total is optional: cursor pagination does not track a page position, and computing a separate exact count adds work. A continuation cue or approximate total can suit feeds and load-more UIs; offset pagination remains useful when users need arbitrary page jumps. (high confidence)

`estimatedDocumentCount()` reads collection metadata and does not accept a query filter. It is faster than an accurate count, so it can provide a rough unfiltered collection total but cannot provide the filtered total for a search or list view. (high confidence)

$facet can return a page branch and a count branch from the same aggregation input. The page branch's $skip/$limit does not cap the count branch, which must count all documents that pass the preceding filter; one aggregation request therefore does not make an exact total free. (high confidence)
MongoDB limits each `$facet` stage's result to 100 MB, does not let `allowDiskUse` lift that limit, and still applies the 16 MiB BSON limit to the final output document. (low confidence)

Published workload reports do not establish a universal latency winner between $facet and separate page/count operations: a .NET benchmark reported the separate path faster, its author reported $facet faster in a JavaScript shell, and a later test found the winner changed with whether its filter was indexed. Benchmark the actual pipeline, driver, and indexes. (medium confidence)

If the interface needs only a next-page indicator, request pageSize + 1 results, return the first pageSize, and set hasNext from whether the extra result exists. This avoids computing a full total and total-page count. (medium confidence)

For a frequently read total over a well-defined subset, a cached or maintained counter can replace repeated counting, but writes must update it and the application should periodically reconcile it against the collection count. (medium confidence)

For an exact unfiltered collection count, `countDocuments({})` can perform a full collection scan. MongoDB documents an `_id_` index hint or an `_id >= MinKey` predicate as ways to use an index for this empty-filter case. (high confidence)
